clue.text: It's turned back at nameless country's border

indicators.note: turned back says the word It is read from right to left

parts.note: the clue word taken as written

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the usual abbreviation for name, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: Denmark is a country

explanation.surface: Something has been sent back at the frontier of an unnamed nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N (name) from DENMARK, leaving DEMARK; 'turned back' gives TI from It.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line left on a shore at high water, so it forms a border between wet and dry ground.

clue.text: Tragic lover man's wager finally came first

indicators.note: the final letter of the phrase is moved round to stand at the front

parts.note: his is the possessive belonging to a man
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A doomed romantic's gamble on a horse eventually won the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally came first' moves the last letter T of HISBET to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Thisbe is the doomed lover of Pyramus in Ovid's tale, both dying in a tragic misunderstanding.

clue.text: Outcome of sadism — a yell of distress

indicators.note: outcome is read as what comes out of these words, so the letters are taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Cruelty produces a scream of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a feeling of alarm and upset, a synonym for distress used as a noun.

clue.text: Seasonal gift from Gaff's car hire start-up

parts.note: the setter Gaff speaking of himself would say my
RR is short for a Rolls-Royce car

indicators.note: start-up asks for the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The setter's Christmas present comes from a new car rental business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaff's' is the setter's own name, so it means MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrrh was one of the three gifts of the Magi, so it is a Christmas-season present.

clue.text: Makes good salesmen, recruiting half-cousin

indicators.note: recruiting means the salesmen take another piece into their midst

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

indicators.note: half asks for the first three of the six letters of cousin

explanation.surface: A sales team hires a relative to make their business profitable.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to make them good, recovering what was spent.

clue.text: A third of directors did seem initially in disagreement

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A third of the board members seemed to be at loggerheads at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at odds is an idiom for quarrelling or disagreeing.

clue.text: Adventurous American boy reported to Lady Godiva?

indicators.note: reported means the words are spoken and we enter what they sound like

parts.note: what might be said to Lady Godiva after her naked ride: Peeping Tom saw you

explanation.surface: Someone tells the naked rider of Coventry that a boy has been watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says a tailor called Peeping Tom spied on Lady Godiva as she rode naked through Coventry; 'Tom saw yer' is the spoken version.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's adventurous boy hero from the Mississippi.

clue.text: Broadcast song when following London bum

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the sound of the phrase gives the letters

parts.note: the Londonderry Air is a song; the part following London is Derry Air

explanation.surface: A tune is played on the radio after a London street scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The Londonderry Air is the Irish tune of Danny Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Derriere is a genteel French borrowing for the backside, which a bum is in British slang.

clue.text: Without speaking trash, left in style

indicators.note: to trash something is to wreck it, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quietly rubbishes a political leftist with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trash' looks like a noun but signals the anagram of L, IN and STYLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something silently means doing it without any sound or talking.

clue.text: In December, force abolished first team coach

parts.note: inst. means of the present month, so a letter dated in December uses it for December
the RUC, Royal Ulster Constabulary, was a police force replaced in 2001

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word team

explanation.surface: During the winter, an axed police force sought a new team manager.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is old commercial shorthand for this month. The RUC was Northern Ireland's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to teach or train them, which is what instructing means.

clue.text: Bacchanal extremes leave royal residence valueless

indicators.note: leave tells us the chosen letters depart from the residence

parts.note: Balmoral is the British royal family's Scottish castle

indicators.note: extremes asks for the first and last letters of Bacchanal

explanation.surface: Drunken excesses leave a palace with no worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters B and L of Bacchanal are removed from BALMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking moral principles, so having no values in the ethical sense.

clue.text: Smile of support

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder that holds up a structure

explanation.surface: A grin of encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a broad grin, and a structural girder carrying a load.

clue.text: Scarf you see reduced in craft store

parts.note: a boa is a long fluffy scarf
thou is the old form of you

indicators.note: reduced means the word see is cut short by a letter

parts.note: the clue word taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper spots a scarf going cheap in a handicraft shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' means boats, not handicrafts.
explanation.definitionFit: A boathouse is a shed where boats, or craft, are stored.

clue.text: Sign member has strain at noon

parts.note: a strain is a tune, and an aria is a solo song

explanation.surface: A zodiac follower is under pressure at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arian is a person born under Aries, so a member of that star sign.

clue.text: Bloomer — short platform

indicators.note: short means the flower's name loses its final letter

parts.note: a daisy is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A blunder on a stubby stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake or a loaf, but here it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall, a platform for speakers.

clue.text: Instruction to rank in reverse at finish

definitions.text: Instruction to rank in reverse at finish

parts.words: Instruction to rank in reverse at finish
parts.note: a drill command telling a line of soldiers to turn and face the opposite way at the end of a manoeuvre

explanation.definitionFit: This military order makes troops turn round completely, hence also a total reversal of opinion.

clue.text: Teresa could be speaking of office

parts.note: Theresa May, the British politician, is one person with this surname
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A politician talks about her ministerial job.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was then Home Secretary, later UK Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayoral describes the office of a mayor, so it relates to a civic post.

clue.text: Cranks see Dr Who was generous

indicators.note: to crank is to turn a handle, so these letters are wound round into a new order

explanation.surface: Eccentrics watch the time-travelling television doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cranks' looks like a noun meaning oddballs, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who showered others with gifts gave lavishly, which is being generous.

clue.text: Novel rock and roll bothering centre left

indicators.note: to rock and roll is to sway about, so the letters are shaken into a new order
centre left means the middle letter of bothering is left out

explanation.surface: An unusual rock-and-roll act is disturbing the moderate left of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre left' removes E, the middle of BOTHERING; 'rock and roll' shuffles the remaining BOTHRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton Rock is a Graham Greene novel, and the clue's 'Novel rock' points at that title.

clue.text: Keep time to retain supporter's backing

indicators.note: to retain is to hold inside, so the time period holds another piece

parts.note: an hour is a period of time

indicators.note: backing means the supporter's word is read backwards

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: Keep the clock running so a fan can keep backing their team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a fan but is a piece of underwear; 'backing' looks like support but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour something is to keep or shelter it, as in harbouring a grudge.

clue.text: Ready for farewell at the end

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a farewell to the dead

indicators.note: end asks for the final letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Prepared to say goodbye at the very last.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe fruit is ready to eat, so the word means ready.

clue.text: Past Times solver's announced

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken and we write what it sounds like

parts.note: the solver is you, so the solver's thing is yours

explanation.surface: The solver's old copies of The Times are mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but just means eras.
explanation.definitionFit: Yore means long ago, as in days of yore, so it names times gone by.

clue.text: Supporter wearing white rose to risky caper

indicators.note: a caper is a playful leap, so these letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan in a floral buttonhole goes on a dangerous escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses pitted York (white rose) against Lancaster (red rose).
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan of the House of York in the Wars of the Roses wore its white rose emblem.

clue.text: Display quality coat in viewing

definitions.meaning: Apple brands its high-resolution screens with this name
the light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye

explanation.surface: A screen's sharpness is shown in a fashion show coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Apple's high-definition screen brand, and the eye's inner light-sensing layer.

clue.text: Tiny little number, one

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
wee again, also meaning small

explanation.surface: A very small song, just one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' is a nursery euphemism for passing water, with the comma only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is childish slang for urinating, which is the same as the baby-talk term.

clue.text: Island's importance egg-head's missing

indicators.note: missing means the named letter is gone from the word for importance

parts.note: weight is importance or significance

indicators.note: head asks for the opening letter of egg

explanation.surface: An island's significance is lost without its brainy residents.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the head of 'egg', leaves WEIGHT. The Isle of Wight is an island off southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight is an island in the English Channel off Hampshire, known as the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: "Carry On" inherently entertaining at any time

indicators.note: entertaining is used as holding a guest, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: per se means in itself, intrinsically
ever means at any time

explanation.surface: The Carry On comedy films are always amusing at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are long-running British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to keep going despite difficulties, which is to persist.

clue.text: Fearful anger in mid-week uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read from bottom to top
in places the anger inside the other letters
mid asks for the middle two letters of week

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A frightening outbreak of rage happens halfway through the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-week' gives the two middle letters of week; in a down entry 'uprising' reads the whole result from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening, so something fearful in that sense.

clue.text: Tradition from the east puts centre into retreat

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left
into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a lair is a hidden den or retreat

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle two letters of puts

explanation.surface: An Eastern custom sends the middle of things into withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' looks like a geographical tag on the tradition, but in an across entry it means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual is a customary ceremony repeated by tradition.

clue.text: Support survey enjoyed on the front in 18, for example

definitions.text: enjoyed on the front in 18, for example

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
to view is to survey

explanation.surface: A support study enjoyed by the seaside in a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is BRIGHTON, a seaside resort with a famous pier; 'the front' is the seafront.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside promenade in Brighton gives a pleasant sight of its pier.

clue.text: Threat of terminal road rage

indicators.note: terminal asks for the last letter of road

parts.note: anger is rage

explanation.surface: Road rage is a menace.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger is a threat or hazard to safety.

clue.text: Basic accommodation from crooked travel agencies Calvin vetoed

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
vetoed means the letters of the name Calvin are barred from the mix

explanation.surface: Cheap rooms from dishonest travel firms that a man called Calvin blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, A, L, V, I, N from TRAVEL AGENCIES and rearrange TREAGEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest passenger class on a ship, offering basic quarters.
